This summer, I worked with Bucknell Professor Sara Stoudt to create an updated version of the National Institute of Science and Technology (NIST) Uncertainty Machine.  The original machine was created "to evaluate the measurement uncertainty associated with a scalar or vectorial output quantity that is a known and explicit function of a set of scalar input quantities for which estimates and evaluations of measurement uncertainty are available."  Prof. Stoudt and I were tasked with recreating the machine in R Shiny for more secure deployment and to take advantage of all that R Shiny has to offer.  Our time frame was small, having only two weeks in August to work on the app before the start of the fall semester.  However, we made great progress before turning it over to other app developers.  The project was split into parts, and Prof. Stoudt and I were in charge of building a user interface that resembled the UI of the original website.  The finished application is not ready yet, but it should be finished soon.  See the attached link to view the original NIST Uncertainty Machine and the format we were tasked with emulating.
